title: RTL: CPU D-cache caches MMIO region — peripheral access broken at SoC level
description: M9 periph-loopback test (claude_verilog_test-k12) revealed: rv32i_core u_dcache (write-back, rv32i_core.sv:812) caches ALL dmem addresses with no uncached/device region. FIX (architectural): add an uncached MMIO window (>=0x2000_0000 peripheral+debug region) decoded in the CPU dmem path so those accesses bypass the D-cache straight to AXI. Requires architecture decision + RTL. Delegate to chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator.

title: Sky130 SoC Stage-2: setup fails at ss corner (WNS -8.9ns); sign-off gated to tt only
description:
Found 2026-07-28 auditing run RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57. At 65 MHz (CLOCK_PERIOD 15.385 ns) the SoC closes setup at tt and ff but FAILS at all three ss corners: max_ss_100C_1v60 WNS -8.902 ns / TNS -118.16 ns; nom_ss -7.767; min_ss -6.386. Checker.SetupViolations reports 'No setup violations found' ONLY because pnr/sky130/soc/config.json sets TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS=['*tt*'] — STA_CORNERS runs all 9, but the gate ignores ss and ff. So the 'Stage-2 signed off at 65 MHz' claim is tt-only and should be stated that way.

ROOT CAUSE: the CPU hard macro's characterized clk->Q. Worst ss path is u_cpu/clk_i -> u_cpu/axi_araddr_o[15] = 8.155 ns, i.e. 53% of the 15.385 ns period consumed inside the macro before any SoC logic runs. The 12 worst ss paths are all u_cpu -> u_cpu or *_ -> u_cpu. This is bead 1ls (GH #123) resurfacing at the slow corner: 4.55 ns clk->Q at nom_tt, 7.54 at nom_ss, 8.12 at max_ss, against a 2.0 ns set_output_delay budget in pnr/sky130/cpu/constraints/sky130_cpu.sdc that gives the optimizer no pressure.

CONTEXT: 1ls was closed 2026-07-25 with 'Accepted 65 MHz (user decision)' after proving budget tightening is a dead end (8.0 ns budget failed to close Stage-1: WNS -2.950, 4826 hold endpoints). That decision was about not reaching 75 MHz — it did NOT establish that ss fails outright at 65 MHz. This bead records that distinct fact so it is not lost.

OPTIONS: (a) document the tt-only position explicitly and keep 65 MHz — cheapest, but then Sky130 Stage-2 is not a true multi-corner sign-off; (b) drop the SoC clock to ~41 MHz (1/(15.385+8.902)) so ss closes honestly; (c) re-harden the Stage-1 CPU macro against an ss-aware budget — 1ls suggests this is very hard for this topology. NOTE the ss numbers are honest for the CPU macro (9 per-corner CPU libs staged 2026-07-25, commit 86e89c1) but the SRAM macro is still TT-only analytical (bead o1i / GH #120), so the ss result carries some SRAM-model error. DECISION NEEDED — not PD tuning.
notes: DECIDED 2026-07-28 (user): option (b) — drop the SoC clock so the ss corner closes honestly, accepting the lower headline frequency in exchange for a genuine across-corner sign-off. Target ~25.0 ns / 40 MHz (arithmetic minimum is 15.385+8.902 = 24.287 ns = 41.17 MHz; extra headroom because a relaxed period lets the optimizer downsize cells and delay grows back). TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS must be widened from ['*tt*'] so ss and ff are actually gated — the tt-only gate is what hid this failure. Folded into the in-flight antenna re-run (bead 58q) so one multi-hour cycle serves both fixes; physical-design-orchestrator notified mid-run. Caveat to carry into the result: CPU macro has real 9-corner libs (86e89c1) but the SRAM macro is still TT-only analytical (o1i / GH #120), so ss numbers carry some SRAM-model error.

title: Sky130 CPU Stage-1: RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR is false — same unrepaired over-cap nets as the SoC had
description: pnr/sky130/cpu/config.json:102 has RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR: false, the same setting that on the SoC (pnr/sky130/soc/config.json) left a 0.626 pF / 1.687 ns-slew net unrepaired and cost 1.03 ns on a macro clk->Q arc. Enabling it on the SoC (bead y7v, commit 1ef3426) recovered setup from -1.4304 to +1.3873 -- +1.15 ns better than the pre-existing baseline -- because it also repaired other over-cap/over-slew nets that had gone unrepaired for the whole Stage-2 history. The Stage-1 CPU hardening run has never had this step enabled, so rv32i_cpu_top's internal nets likely carry the same unrepaired slew/cap violations. Its .lib is not WRONG (arcs are characterized from the actual netlist) but is probably pessimistic, and the SoC consumes that .lib as a hard macro whose output drive cannot be resized. NOTE enabling it will likely hit the same RSZ-0090 abort if any macro .lib in the CPU flow declares an unachievable max_transition -- the SRAM fix was 8b11092. Also note the SoC antenna cost: pin violations went 144 -> 164 when this was enabled (bead 58q). Precedent: all ASAP7 configs run with this true.
notes: 2026-07-27 FINAL — RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57 COMPLETE, adoption fully validated on every axis vs the previously published closure RUN_2026-07-26_16-05-43. TIMING, all three gated *tt* corners improved on BOTH setup and hold: setup nom_tt +1.3873->+1.8585 (+0.471), min_tt +2.5656->+2.8940 (+0.328), max_tt +0.3391->+0.8662 (+0.527); hold nom_tt +0.1444->+0.2932 (+0.149), min_tt +0.2489->+0.2919 (+0.043), max_tt +0.0923->+0.2706 (+0.178). Violator list EMPTY, and both Checker.SetupViolations and Checker.HoldViolations were LIVE GATES for this run. LVS 'Circuits match uniquely'. KLayout DRC 4 and Magic DRC 9081, both identical to baseline. ANTENNA IMPROVED 164->147 pin and 134->127 net -- I had predicted a regression there (design repair cost +20 pin at SoC and +4 at CPU previously); the better-repaired macro actually reduced it. max_tt, the tightest corner and the one where the CPU macro STILL violates setup internally at -0.12078, gained the most setup and nearly tripled hold margin, so that residual macro violation does not propagate to the SoC. CONCLUSION: the 0ro premise is confirmed end-to-end -- unrepaired over-cap/over-slew nets in the Stage-1 CPU made its .lib arcs pessimistic, and repairing them improves everything downstream. Macro views staged in commit 995c487, merged to main via PR #125.

title: SRAM_SKY130 hard-macro branch not covered by default regression
description:
tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile defaults SRAM_TARGET=freepdk45, and the soc_all target invokes sram_controller without SRAM_TARGET=sky130. So the OpenRAM hard-macro read path in rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv (rd_pend_q pipeline + 2-entry skid buffer handling the macro's 1-cycle registered read latency) is only exercised by a separate manual invocation.

Evidence: Stage-2 sign-off reported soc_all 99/99 AND sky130-branch 11/11 as two distinct runs, not one.

Risk: the SRAM_SKY130 branch can silently bit-rot on future unrelated RTL changes, since nothing in routine regression touches it. This is the branch that carried a P0 data-corruption bug (rvalid asserted one cycle before the macro's negedge-launched dout1 latched) found on 2026-07-24 - exactly the class of defect that must not regress unnoticed.

Fix options: add a soc_all_sky130 target, or make soc_all run the sram_controller suite twice (both SRAM_TARGET values), or add a CI job.
close_reason: Verified: tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile soc_all now runs sram_controller twice (default flat freepdk45 + SRAM_TARGET=sky130 OpenRAM macro branch). Full soc_all re-run: 18 suite invocations, 110/110 tests PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, exit 0. sky130 sram_controller pass = 11/11, confirmed built with +define+SRAM_SKY130 -GMEM_WORDS=1024 and sim/sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8.sv (not a silent flat-array fallback). No ordering/stale-sim_build issue running sram_controller twice back-to-back. Log: /nobackup/soc_all_gh104/soc_all_68m_run1.log. design_state.json history[] + memory/verification/experiences.jsonl updated.

title: GH #104: sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 has 4 KLayout DRC violations (upstream OpenRAM generator)
description:
Full-deck KLayout DRC (sky130A_mr.drc) on the Stage-2 SoC sign-off GDS (RUN_2026-07-24_09-58-19) found 4 real violations, all inside the OpenRAM-compiled sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 macro's own internal cells. Confirmed via an isolation test (full KLayout deck on the macro's raw standalone GDS, no SoC context): identical violations, identical coordinates -- proving these are baked into the OpenRAM compile itself, not caused by or fixable via SoC-level PDN/floorplan/routing work.

Violations:
- m2.2 (met2 spacing <0.14um) x1, cell ..._wmask_dff, measured 0.055um (~60% short of spec)
- via2.2 (via2 spacing <0.2um) x2, cells macro-top + ..._bank, measured 0.125um (~37.5% short)
- m3.2 (met3 spacing <0.3um) x1, cell ..._bank, measured 0.29um (~3% short, ~1nm, plausibly grid-rounding but still non-conformant)

Root cause: the macro was compiled views-first with check_lvsdrc=False (OpenRAM's own DRC/LVS never ran), a deliberate choice made after the check_lvsdrc=True extraction died to a host reboot at ~7h. Confirmed these are in OpenRAM's generated assembly layer (compiler/modules/bank.py + the generic dff_array factory type used as wmask_dff), not a foundry-drawn primitive -- searched the installed sky130_fd_bd_sram primitive library, zero matches for these cell names.

USER DECISION (2026-07-24): accept + document for now, do not patch the GDS, do not retry OpenRAM config, do not attempt a DRC-clean regenerate at this time. Full record: pnr/sky130/soc/pdn.tcl (header comment) and memory/pd/run_state.md.

Follow-up: a future DRC-clean macro regeneration (options considered: (a) check_lvsdrc=True regen -- high non-completion risk given reboot cadence, and wouldn't fix anything by itself since OpenRAM geometry is deterministic, only reports; (b) OpenRAM config tweak, e.g. different words_per_row/column-mux, that might shift the bank/wmask_dff floorplan to avoid these spots -- speculative, ~190min+ per rebuild attempt; (c) targeted GDS patch of the 4 exact coordinates -- fast but fragile/non-reproducible from config).

Full-chip DRC signoff for GH #104 is NOT complete until this is resolved or explicitly re-accepted at tape-out-readiness review.
notes: Tracked on GitHub: https://github.com/chuanseng-ng/claude_verilog_test/issues/121
close_reason: Won't-fix, accepted with evidence (GH #121). efabless prebuilt sky130_sram_2kbyte_1rw1r_32x512_8 -- used in real MPW silicon -- ships 32 magic DRC errors in its own OpenRAM build log and is likewise analytical + nominal-corner-only; repo has no 4KB 32x1024_8 variant to swap to. Our 4 violations (one ~1nm) are OpenRAM generator norm, not a consequence of check_lvsdrc=False (geometry is deterministic; the checker only reports). All fix options cost 190min+/attempt on a host rebooting every 2-8h for no correctness gain. Re-open trigger: genuine tape-out-readiness review.

title: Sky130 Stage 2: CPU-macro + peripherals SoC, real DRC/LVS (GH #104)
design:
GH #104, part of epic #102 (bead n0i). Stage 2: pnr/sky130/soc/ — CPU as hard macro (Stage-1 native Sky130 views) + flat peripherals, NO GPU, real Magic DRC + KLayout DRC + Netgen LVS. Template = pnr/asap7/soc/ (adapt ASAP7->Sky130, drop GPU, flip DRC/LVS true).

APPROACH (PD-only; no functional RTL change):
- GPU exclusion = TIE-OFF STUB (not RTL surgery). Swap rtl/gpu/gpu_top.sv for a synthesizable stub driving all AXI master + irq outputs idle/0; soc_top.sv UNCHANGED. GPU optimizes away; crossbar keeps idle GPU master ports. Zero RTL re-verification (preserves soc_all 82/82). Drop rtl/gpu/* + gpu_pkg from the sv2v file list, add the tie-off stub.
- CPU = hard macro: blackbox stub at synth (rv32i_cpu_top_stub.sv) + Stage-1 native Sky130 views at P&R (pnr/sky130/cpu/macro/rv32i_cpu_top.{lef,lib,nl.v.gz}). CPU macro = VPWR/VGND PG pins, 3600x1800um.
- SoC SRAM (sram_controller, 4KB) + boot_rom (4KB): keep BEHAVIORAL (flat flops ~32K each -> ~25-30K cells total). 'flat peripherals' per issue; avoids a 2nd SRAM-macro Magic artifact. Note added die area.
- sv2v frontend (soc-synth-needs-sv2v): new make sky130-soc-sv2v target, SV file list = ASAP7 list minus GPU + the tie-off stub; json_header_soc.py workaround for soc_top port stub.

FILES TO CREATE (pnr/sky130/soc/): config.json, constraints/sky130_soc.sdc, pdn.tcl, macro_placement.cfg, gpu_top_tieoff.sv, rv32i_cpu_top_stub.sv, soc_top_ports.v, json_header_soc.py, gen scripts; pnr/Makefile targets sky130-soc-sv2v + librelane-sky130-soc.

KEY CONFIG:
- Clock ~75 MHz (Sky130 CPU ceiling; no GPU governing). Apply set_driving_cell on inputs (Stage-1/CodeRabbit lesson) for honest timing.
- Die: must exceed CPU macro 3600x1800 + flat logic; est ~5000x2400um, util ~40-50%. PD agent to size.
- PDN: sky130 met1-5 grid + CPU macro M4/M5 ring; PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS=".*u_cpu.* VPWR VGND vccd1 vssd1"; PDN_CONNECT_MACROS_TO_GRID=true.
- RUN_MAGIC_DRC=true, RUN_KLAYOUT_DRC=true, RUN_LVS=true.
- CPU macro in MACROS object (Stage-1 lesson) so Magic DRC blackboxes it (avoid flattening macro GDS -> phantom li.3). EXTRA_SPICE_MODELS = CPU macro spice + any SRAM spice for Netgen LVS.
- Portable pdk_dir:: paths (CodeRabbit lesson). GPL/DPL_CELL_PADDING=4 (Stage-1 lesson).

RISKS: (1) CPU-macro Magic DRC artifact (same class as Stage-1 SRAM; KLayout authoritative). (2) Behavioral SoC SRAM/ROM flop area bloats die. (3) LVS needs CPU macro spice/netlist + correct PG. (4) sv2v file-list drift. (5) CPU macro PG (VPWR/VGND) -> SoC PDN connection correctness (floating-domain risk).

GATE: KLayout DRC=0, Netgen LVS=MATCH, Magic DRC (expect macro artifact -> documented, KLayout authoritative), timing met @~75MHz honest (with set_driving_cell), PDN connected (CPU macro powered). Record fmax/power/area + DRC/LVS logs.

EXECUTION: chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator (read PD memories + knowledge.md first). PD-only -> no functional re-verification.
notes:
2026-07-29 CORRECTION to the 2026-07-28 antenna analysis above — that breakdown was WRONG, read the corrected numbers here instead.

Error 1 (report): I analysed 39-openroad-repairantennas/2-openroad-checkantennas/ (89 rows / 56 nets), which is the IN-FLIGHT PRE-DRT check. The report matching manufacturability.rpt's 147/127 is 44-openroad-checkantennas-1/reports/antenna_summary.rpt (149 rows), POST-DRT and final. DRT measurably reshuffles violators between the two — net578/net608 and several other nets I cited do not appear in the final list at all.

Error 2 (attribution): my 'violators are overwhelmingly the CPU<->bus AXI nets' claim does not survive against the final report. Resolving all 127 violating nets to their physical driver pin in the flattened post-route netlist gives:
    plain standard-cell logic/flop (crossbar, DMA, APB, sram_controller glue; no macro pin)  123  82.6%
    CPU macro pin WITH ANTENNADIFFAREA                                                        19  12.8%
    CPU macro pin MISSING ANTENNADIFFAREA                                                      4   2.7%
    SRAM macro pin (no antenna props at all)                                                   2   1.3%
    top-level port (clk_i, unprotected)                                                        1   0.7%
So this is ordinary long-route antenna exposure on a 6700x3100 um die, NOT a macro-abstract problem.

Error 3 (LEF gap not a defect): all 95 CPU output pins missing ANTENNADIFFAREA trace deterministically to sky130_fd_sc_hd__conb_1 constant-tie cells. VERIFIED: the vendor's own sky130_fd_sc_hd.lef publishes no ANTENNA properties on conb_1's HI/LO pins either. Upstream SkyWater library convention, not a Magic/LibreLane/project defect — regenerating the abstract would reproduce it identically. Hand-patching rejected (no real value to copy; the 2 actually-violating such pins run up to 11.4x over, far beyond what a tie cell's diffusion could close). SRAM macro LEF has zero antenna properties on any pin (OpenRAM/PDK-vendor limitation, out of scope).

Error 4 (die): 6700x3100 um, not 4557x4557 — I wrongly assumed square from design__die__area = 20,770,000 um2.

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE FOUND: pnr/sky130/soc/config.json was missing four antenna-repair keys that the CPU/SRAM/GPU configs all set, so the SoC had been running antenna repair on weaker-than-default settings. Added in commit 29cb64a: RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION=true, GRT_ANTENNA_ITERS=8, GRT_ANTENNA_MARGIN=25, DIODE_ON_PORTS='in'. Same commit applies the ujv clock relax (CLOCK_PERIOD 15.385 -> 25.0 ns) and widens TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS ['*tt*'] -> ['*'].

title: apb4_register_bank: range check truncates N_REGS at max bank size (GH #87)
description: CodeRabbit follow-up PR #84, pre-existing latent edge. WORDW'(N_REGS) cast wraps to 0 when N_REGS==2**WORDW exactly -> write/read guards reject every access at max bank size. Latent today: all banks N_REGS<2**WORDW. Phase 6 adds ~6 new peripheral banks that could hit max. FIX: compare addr_word against integer-sized N_REGS first, then slice for indexing (write+read paths). RTL->rtl-design-orchestrator, verify apb4_register_bank unit suite + soc_all.
close_reason: Fixed — rtl/soc/apb4_register_bank.sv:102,117 zero-extend addr_word to 32b before comparing against N_REGS ({{(32-WORDW){1'b0}}, addr_word} < N_REGS), so N_REGS==2**WORDW no longer wraps to 0. Comment at :100 documents the truncating-cast bug. GH #87.

title: axil_to_apb: gate ARREADY against concurrent AW/W in S_IDLE (GH #85)
description: CodeRabbit follow-up PR #84, pre-existing latent. In S_IDLE with AWVALID+WVALID+ARVALID all asserted, write wins state_d but AR capture overwrites addr_q/is_write_q -> accepted write lost or wrong-channel response. Latent today: CPU D-cache never issues concurrent R+W. Phase 6 adds AES/NPU/DMA masters that can. FIX: gate s_axil_arready with && !s_axil_awvalid && !s_axil_wvalid (axil_to_apb.sv:133) + directed AR+AW+W concurrent test. RTL->rtl-design-orchestrator, verify axil_to_apb unit suite + soc_all.
close_reason: Fixed — rtl/soc/axil_to_apb.sv:138 gates s_axil_arready with && !s_axil_awvalid && !s_axil_wvalid, so a concurrent AR+AW+W in S_IDLE cannot overwrite addr_q/is_write_q. GH #85 rationale documented in-line at :133-137.

title: PLL safety: clearing pll_enable (CONTROL[0]) self-bricks the SoC
description: CodeRabbit (PR #88) MAJOR, pre-existing (not introduced by the pll_subsystem refactor; same gating in old pll_axil_regs). pll_enable=CONTROL[0] in pll_apb_regs (clk_i domain, reset default=1). If firmware clears it: pll_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_enable->0 -> PLL held in reset -> pll_locked->0 -> core_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_locked->0 -> resets CPU+soc_bus. pll_apb_regs is NOT reset by core_rst_n (clk_i domain) so pll_enable stays 0 -> permanent deadlock; the APB master that wrote 0 is gone before it can write 1 back. FIX OPTIONS: (a) make CONTROL[0] set-only / non-clearable in SoC integration (firmware can enable, not disable); or (b) gate PLL reconfig so it doesn't drop core_rst_n in a non-recoverable way; or (c) add a startup/watchdog recovery. Functional design change -> own PR + soc_all re-verify. Natural to fold into #4 (3-PLL/CDC) where PLL control is reworked. NOT fixed in the refactor PR #88 (which preserved existing behavior).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #108 — CONTROL[0] non-clearable (WMASK 03F1->03F0)

title: Sky130 CPU Stage-1: Magic DRC reports 27.7M li.3 violations — never passed, likely LEF-abstract artifact
description: Every Sky130 Stage-1 CPU run reports Magic DRC errors: 27733913 — BIT-IDENTICAL between RUN_2026-07-21_18-02-11 and RUN_2026-07-27_05-52-19, so it is systematic and deterministic, not caused by any recent change. KLayout DRC on the same runs is 0 and Netgen LVS says 'Circuits match uniquely', which makes the Magic result the odd one out. The report (*-magic-drc/reports/drc_violations.magic.rpt, 27.7M lines) is dominated by 'Local interconnect spacing < 0.17um (li.3)' with roughly a dozen other rule types present (licon.1, licon.5a, licon.8, licon.8a, poly.2/4/7/8, psd.10b, nwell.4). PRIME SUSPECT: pnr/sky130/cpu/config.json sets MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: false, so Magic runs DRC on the LEF/DEF-derived view where the sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 macro is an abstract black box rather than real GDS geometry — a classic source of spurious li spacing errors at macro boundaries. Worth testing MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: true on one run to confirm before treating any of these as real. CONSEQUENCE: Stage-1 CPU has never had a genuine Magic DRC sign-off, and that gap is inherited by everything consuming the rv32i_cpu_top macro.
notes: 2026-07-27 HYPOTHESIS REFUTED — RUN_2026-07-27_20-33-10 with MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=true. Magic DRC COUNT = 27,730,498 with REAL GDS vs 27,733,913 with the LEF abstract. Difference 3,415, about 0.01 percent — essentially IDENTICAL. The li.3 violations are NOT a macro-boundary/LEF-abstract artifact; they persist when Magic reads actual geometry. Same rule families in both reports (licon.1, licon.5a, licon.8a, poly.2/4/7/8, psd.10b). So Stage-1 CPU has a real, large, systematic DRC condition that needs its own root-cause, not a reporting artifact. IMPORTANT SCALE CORRECTION from the magic log: '[INFO] COUNT: 27730498' is followed by '[INFO] Should be divided by 3 or 4' — Magic counts each violation 3-4x, so distinct violations are roughly 6.9M-9.2M, still enormous. SECONDARY FINDING, and the reason the config was reverted: MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=true is NOT USABLE on this design. Magic hits fatal 'Unknown layer/datatype in boundary' errors reading the PDK SRAM macro's internal cells (sky130_fd_bd_sram__openram_dp_cell*, layers 235/0, 33/42, 33/43, 22/21, 22/22) and LibreLane aborts the whole flow with 'Encountered one or more fatal errors while running Magic'. The DRC itself completed and wrote its report BEFORE the abort, which is how we got the number. NOT an OOM — RAM went 11G->13G at death, no memory pressure; the magic-drc step ran 42 min (21:37->22:19). Config reverted to false so future CPU runs are not broken. NEXT STEPS if this is picked up: (a) sample actual li.3 coordinates to see whether they cluster inside the SRAM macro footprint or spread across the standard-cell array; (b) check whether the sky130A Magic tech file version matches what the PDK SRAM GDS expects, since the unknown layer/datatype errors suggest a tech-file/GDS mismatch that could also explain spurious li.3; (c) compare against the Sky130 SoC run, which reports only 9081 Magic DRC errors on a LARGER die — that asymmetry is a strong clue and worth explaining.
close_reason: RESOLVED — PDK SRAM macro artifact, WAIVED. Exhaustive streaming classification of all 27,730,498 coordinates in RUN_2026-07-27_20-33-10/63-magic-drc: 27,730,498/27,730,498 = 100.0000% lie inside the 10 sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 footprints; 0 in the routing channel, 0 in the standard-cell logic zone (max y = 907.87um; logic zone starts at 917.5um). All 26 rule families are 100% SRAM-internal — none leak outside; li.3 (922,628) is not even the dominant family (diff/tap.9 3.0M, licon.1 2.6M, li.1 2.3M). Reproduced independently twice with separate awk passes. SoC/CPU asymmetry explained: SoC declares the CPU as a hard MACROS entry with MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=false, so read_macro_lef loads the LEF abstract and Magic never touches SRAM-internal geometry — its 9,081 errors are a disjoint set (9,049 nwell.4 + 32 met4.4a), the already-documented DEF+LEF-abstract artifact class, not a diluted CPU flood. KLayout=0 on identical GDS because sky130A_mr.drc has explicit hierarchy-aware SRAM_EXCLUDE (select("-*sky130_sram_*kbyte_*") off nsdm/psdm/nwell, grouping the SRAM with I/O pad cells as a pre-verified macro) plus a working areaid:ce two-tier li1 scope — the relief Magic's COREID/coreli attempts but fails to deliver for this OpenRAM macro. Root cause: Magic's flat drc(full) engine cannot validate this dense custom OpenRAM macro's internals, independent of read path. Stage-1 sign-off stands on KLayout DRC=0 + Netgen LVS MATCH + DRT 0. Secondary techfile layer/datatype gap filed as y0w. Full write-up in memory/pd/run_state.md.

title: GH #123: CPU macro clk->Q on AXI outputs 4.55ns @nom_tt -- Stage-1 output budget far too loose
description: CORRECTED 2026-07-25 (original premise was wrong). pnr/sky130/cpu/constraints/sky130_cpu.sdc DOES budget I/O: 28 set_input_delay + 38 set_output_delay lines, 2.0ns max each side on the AXI ports. Real root cause is that the budget is TOO LOOSE: set_output_delay -max 2.0 against a 13.333ns period lets the macro take up to 11.33ns to produce an output; it takes 4.55ns @nom_tt (7.54 @nom_ss, 8.12 @max_ss) so the optimizer had zero pressure to do better. 4.55ns clk->Q at the TYPICAL corner is ~30% of the period gone before the signal leaves the macro. Second independent cause: rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:580-585 early-accept makes arready a combinational function of araddr via decode() + priority arbitration (the 7-gate fabric cone in the worst path). FIX: raise set_output_delay/set_input_delay on AXI ports so the macro must drive outputs in ~4-5ns, re-run librelane-sky130-cpu, confirm it still closes at 13.333ns and clk->Q drops, re-stage 9 corner libs + LEF/GDS, re-run Stage-2 at 75MHz. Only if insufficient, consider registering crossbar arready (costs 1 cycle/read, needs decision + full re-verification).

Tried 2.0->8.0ns on AXI ports (RUN_2026-07-25_19-30-52): Stage-1 failed to close, setup WNS -2.950 on apb_prdata_o[13] (APB budget untouched -- the AXI tightening ate design-wide optimizer headroom), 4826 hold-violating endpoints. SDC REVERTED to 2.0ns. REAL TARGET: crossbar fabric = 8.83ns of the nom_tt path (20 driver stages) vs macro 4.55ns -- the araddr->decode->arbitration->arready early-accept cone at rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:580-585. title: GH #120: SPICE-characterize sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 at ss/ff corners (CPU macro DONE)
description:
Both hard macros used in the Sky130 SoC (rv32i_cpu_top from Stage-1 CPU sign-off, and sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 from the OpenRAM compile) provide only a single characterized Liberty view each: nom_tt_025C_1v80 / TT_1p8V_25C. pnr/sky130/soc/config.json's MACROS entries map that one .lib to every PVT corner via a wildcard ("lib": {"*": [...]}). Confirmed directly from the Stage-2 sign-off run log: analyzing the "nom_ss_100C_1v60" corner literally reads the nom_tt .lib file for both macros' internal timing arcs. Only the sky130_fd_sc_hd standard-cell library genuinely varies by corner in this flow.

Consequence (bidirectional, see constraints/sky130_soc.sdc header and memory/pd/run_state.md for full detail):
- nom_tt results are valid -- the one corner where macro characterization matches the analysis label.
- ss-corner SETUP results that touch either macro boundary are likely OPTIMISTIC (real slow-corner macro delay would be slower than the nom_tt stand-in, so real setup could be worse than reported).
- ss-corner HOLD results that touch either macro boundary are likely PESSIMISTIC (real slow-corner macro delay would be slower, giving more hold margin than reported -- e.g. the residual max_ss hold violation on u_cpu/axi_bready_o, -70.8ps, is plausibly non-existent in real silicon).

This means Stage-2's timing sign-off, as currently constituted, is a TYPICAL-CORNER (nom_tt) sign-off only -- not a validated multi-corner sign-off, despite reporting numbers under ss/ff corner labels.

Fix: characterize both macros at ss/ff corners for real.
- rv32i_cpu_top: re-run the Stage-1 CPU characterization flow at the additional corners (this project's existing flow already supports multi-corner .lib generation for standard PD signoff; the CPU macro was apparently only carried forward with its nom_tt view into the SoC MACROS config).
- sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8: OpenRAM natively supports multi-corner characterization (process_corners/supply_voltages/temperatures config, nominal_corner_only=False) -- our compile used nominal_corner_only=True for speed/risk reasons during the views-first pass. Re-running with full corners would need SPICE-based characterization per corner (not the analytical mode already flagged as broken for power in bead/GH#104 -- see the power-report-garbage finding), likely another multi-hour run with real reboot risk on this host, similar to the check_lvsdrc=True extraction.

Related: this is a SEPARATE issue from claude_verilog_test-0jp (the 4 KLayout DRC violations) -- track independently, though both stem from the same root pattern (views-first/speed-optimized macro compile choices deferring real characterization work).

Not resolved before Stage-2 sign-off; documented and accepted for now per user decision (65 MHz clock relaxation closes nom_tt setup; residual ss-corner setup/hold failures are accepted given the corner-modeling caveat above, not chased with a resizer margin knob).
notes: 2026-07-27 FEASIBILITY VERDICT: NOT FEASIBLE on this host, measured not estimated. Xyce's own progress meter in temp_charretry/spice_stdout.log: 'Percent complete: 17.0783 %' at 05:37:07 with 'Estimated time to completion: 52 min., 33 sec.' => ONE delay simulation ~63 minutes. OpenRAM does NOT run one simulation per corner: delay.py find_feasible_period_one_port is a period-doubling loop capped at 9 iterations (time_out=9), then find_min_period_one_port runs a BINARY SEARCH, repeated per read port -- this macro has 2 read ports (1RW+1R). That is roughly 25-30 full simulations per corner = ~26-31 h/corner, ~80-95 h for the 3 corners, against a host that reboots every 2-8 h and where tmux does not survive. The netlist-only sram_char.py path (which removed the 3.7 h routing per attempt) does not help: the cost is the SPICE search itself. Note sram_char.py forces trim_netlist=False, and the 'trimmed.sp' from the generation run is 4.30 MB vs the full 4.17 MB sram.sp -- trimming is not meaningfully shrinking this 32768-bit array, so there is no easy speedup there. The 05:17 run also died at 17% for an unexplained reason (no kernel OOM in journalctl -k, no systemd-oomd entry, no Python traceback, timing.raw had reached 1.0 GB); that is unresolved but MOOT -- even a clean run cannot fit the search into this host's uptime. RECOMMENDATION: keep both documented hand-patches on the TT lib (zeroed internal_power, max_transition 0.04->0.5), leave the macro analytical + single-corner, and pursue bead 0ro instead. Revisit only with a machine that stays up ~4 days or with a genuinely trimmed/reduced characterization netlist.
